limitations: Work-in-progress technical report; energy claims include estimates and require direct local measurement; dedicated bitnet.cpp runtime is a separate condition.
relevance: Native ternary 2.4B architecture with an official x86/ARM CPU runtime directly tests whether deployment-specific low-bit training beats post-training q4 on the sovereign node.
title: BitNet b1.58 2B4T Technical Report

limitations: Repository commit updates documentation rather than freezing the full runtime release; benchmark results remain tied to paper and local reproduction conditions.
relevance: Pins the dedicated native 1.58-bit CPU/GPU runtime required to test BitNet as a deployment condition.
title: Microsoft BitNet runtime

limitations: Compute-allocation law spans 143M-12.6B training experiments; it does not provide deployment quality, safety, or CPU-energy evidence.
relevance: Gives a principled teacher/student compute-allocation rule and warns that training a teacher for one student can be worse than supervised learning.
title: Distillation Scaling Laws

limitations: QAT and specialized kernels make this a different training/runtime condition from post-training GGUF quantization; CPU ordering must be measured locally.
relevance: Directly qualifies the prior q4 sweet-spot assumption: 2-bit can be competitive when trained and implemented for that bit width.
title: ParetoQ: Improving Scaling Laws in Extremely Low-bit LLM Quantization

limitations: No public model weights or independent CPU/energy measurement; public benchmark claims are first-party and Apple-silicon specific.
relevance: The 3B on-device model combines 2-bit QAT, KV-cache sharing, tool calling, and LoRA adapters; this is method evidence for compression plus specialization, not an ApprenticeOps roster artifact.
title: Apple Intelligence Foundation Language Models: Tech Report 2025

limitations: Gated Gemma license; intended for task-specific fine-tuning rather than dialogue; first-party benchmark and Samsung-device results lack independent replication and energy measurement.
relevance: A 270M specialist baseline with an explicit fine-tuning recipe, no-tool relevance metric, and measured on-device CPU profile is directly testable for narrow typed ops functions.
title: FunctionGemma 270M IT

limitations: Reasoning evidence is benchmark-centric; weights are gated under a noncommercial research license; local CPU runtime support remains unverified.
relevance: Open sub-billion reasoning recipe challenges the assumption that useful reasoning requires >10T pretraining tokens or multi-billion size.
title: MobileLLM-R1: Exploring the Limits of Sub-Billion Language Model Reasoners with Open Training Recipes

limitations: Model card shows CPU loading, not measured CPU performance; benchmark table is first-party; model-card arXiv metadata is defective.
relevance: Apache-2.0 3B attention/Mamba2 hybrid with tool calling and 128K context is a roster-relevant architecture candidate.
title: Granite 4.0 H-Micro

limitations: First-party benchmark claims; CPU loading is supported but CPU latency and energy are not measured; mutable blog corrections demonstrate why the pinned model revision matters.
relevance: A fully open 3B dual-mode model with training mixtures, synthetic-data lineage, tool calling, long-context stages, and merge-based recovery offers unusually strong recipe transparency.
title: SmolLM3 3B

limitations: Mutable first-party blog; claims are not independent; page includes community comments and corrections that are not scientific evidence.
relevance: Captures the full public training recipe and page-level correction history while the immutable model revision anchors artifacts.
title: SmolLM3: smol, multilingual, long-context reasoner

limitations: Edge positioning lacks measured CPU telemetry in the abstract; nominal 3B artifacts can include modality components; each released variant needs actual total-count and runtime verification.
relevance: Cascade distillation produces base, instruct, and reasoning variants at 3B/8B/14B and is directly relevant to training-path comparisons.
title: Ministral 3

limitations: Compression starts from 8B and reports GPU/long-context evidence; the nominal 4B artifact and license need exact verification before roster use.
relevance: Group-aware SSM pruning plus distillation is a training-path comparator for hybrid architectures, not just a model-size result.
title: Minitron-SSM: Efficient Hybrid Language Model Compression through Group-Aware SSM Pruning

limitations: Headline throughput is hardware- and batch-sensitive, primarily H100/Jetson evidence rather than single-request x86 CPU latency; architecture differs from baselines.
relevance: PostNAS hybrid 2B/4B models show that architecture search can move the efficiency frontier, but need local runtime measurements before affecting ApprenticeOps conclusions.
title: Jet-Nemotron: Efficient Language Model with Post Neural Architecture Search

limitations: Insecure-code tuning is a narrow adversarial domain and model-specific; broad transfer to benign ops adaptation must be tested rather than assumed.
relevance: Shows that narrow fine-tuning can produce broad misalignment and supports a full cross-domain safety rerun for every specialist adapter.
title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs

limitations: Outlier samples are adversarially selected rather than random benign adaptation; transfer to ordinary ops corpora remains an experiment.
relevance: Demonstrates that benign-looking data is not a safety guarantee and motivates influence/outlier audits before domain fine-tuning.
title: Benign Samples Matter! Fine-tuning On Outlier Benign Samples Severely Breaks Safety

limitations: Mitigation evidence covers four datasets and larger GPU-oriented models; it cannot replace direct safety/retention evaluation on ApprenticeOps adapters.
relevance: A concrete defended adaptation arm: filter and compensate fine-tuning deltas while retaining utility, followed by independent safety tests.
title: Safe Delta: Consistently Preserving Safety when Fine-Tuning LLMs on Diverse Datasets

limitations: Studies public benchmarks, not private incident holdouts; question-level fidelity/resistance must be adapted to ops scenarios.
relevance: Shows that paraphrase/semantic-preserving benchmark rewrites do not reliably remove contamination and supplies question-level fidelity and resistance metrics.
title: The Emperor's New Clothes in Benchmarking? A Rigorous Examination of Mitigation Strategies for LLM Benchmark Data Contamination

limitations: Forgetting appears after very long continued pretraining; it does not validate short LoRA/SFT runs or unknown proprietary training histories.
relevance: Qualifies a blanket contamination-invalidates-everything claim by showing that repeated contamination can later be forgotten under sufficiently extended training.
title: How Much Can We Forget about Data Contamination?

limitations: The strongest evidence uses multimodal and GPU-scale settings; ApprenticeOps can adopt disjoint-variant analysis but not reproduce the training regime locally.
relevance: Separates SFT's format stabilization from outcome-RL generalization, cautioning against reading in-distribution SFT gains as new capability.
title: SFT Memorizes, RL Generalizes: A Comparative Study of Foundation Model Post-training

limitations: Includes language-model fine-tuning but also simplified generative settings; frontier extrapolation is not established.
relevance: Shows that synthetic-data outcome depends on the workflow: replacement collapses, while accumulating real plus synthetic data remains stable in tested settings.
title: Collapse or Thrive: Perils and Promises of Synthetic Data in a Self-Generating World

limitations: Demonstration uses a two-layer BERT and benchmark-specific transfer; it establishes evaluation vulnerability, not an expected effect size for ops SLMs.
relevance: Teacher-generated data can launder benchmark knowledge into a small student without genuine reasoning, requiring teacher and benchmark lineage metadata.
title: Data Laundering: Artificially Boosting Benchmark Results through Knowledge Distillation

limitations: Main pool uses Llama 3.1 8B and target-task data; a <=5B replication is needed before deployment conclusions.
relevance: Adaptive recycling of nearly 1,000 public LoRAs rarely beat a target LoRA, and random adapters behaved similarly, motivating target and randomized controls.
title: The Appeal and Reality of Recycling LoRAs with Adaptive Merging

limitations: Published evaluation assumes known task identity and does not cover ops safety, contamination, or routing errors.
relevance: Directly CPU-relevant continual adapter-bank design for Llama 1B/Qwen 1.5B under storage limits; suitable as a separate future experiment.
title: K-Merge: Online Continual Merging of Adapters for On-device Large Language Models

limitations: First-party internal Sonnet/Haiku-class experiments with no public checkpoints, code, or independent replication; evidence does not establish transfer to open <=5B models.
relevance: Suggests alignment training should teach reasons/principles and diverse tool contexts, and must be evaluated OOD rather than only against the training distribution.
title: Teaching Claude Why

limitations: Benefits vary by model and task, and full-rank PEFT can train more slowly than LoRA; ops-domain utility, retention, and safety remain untested.
relevance: Shows that LoRA's low-rank update can itself limit adaptation, so rank/update structure must be a preregistered treatment rather than hidden implementation detail.
title: RandLoRA: Full-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large models

limitations: Basic deterministic math tasks do not transfer directly to open-ended ops reasoning; its composite Overthinking Score should not replace failure-inclusive component metrics.
relevance: Provides dynamic deterministic tasks and explicit token-cap collapse evidence to refine reasoning-budget sensitivity analysis.
title: Do LLMs Overthink Basic Math Reasoning? Benchmarking the Accuracy-Efficiency Tradeoff in Language Models

limitations: GPU/vLLM quantization and pruning; local GGUF/CPU transfer is unproven; benchmark composition affects the reported loss.
relevance: Shows compression loss is capability-specific: workflow/tool-use can survive while real application accuracy drops more, motivating task-stratified quant analysis.
title: Can Compressed LLMs Truly Act? An Empirical Evaluation of Agentic Capabilities in LLM Compression

limitations: Repository has no formal release and is GPU/vLLM-oriented; this commit pins the inspected point in time.
relevance: Reproducibility artifact for ACBench's agentic compression tasks.
title: ACBench repository

limitations: Single Raspberry Pi 4, unclear exact repetition count, model-specific timeout adjustments, and filtering malformed/empty responses create comparability and survivorship concerns.
relevance: Direct wall-energy measurements across q-levels show no universal low-bit ordering and motivate exact-lineage q3/q4/q8 replication on the locked node.
title: Sustainable LLM Inference for Edge AI: Evaluating Quantized LLMs for Energy Efficiency, Output Accuracy, and Inference Latency

limitations: One MoE model, two devices, and total size above the <=5B thesis bound; qualitative transfer to older x86 remains untested.
relevance: Directly falsifies active-parameter-only efficiency reasoning on bandwidth-constrained edge hardware and reinforces recording total/resident parameters.
title: Does Mixture-of-Experts Actually Help Inference on Consumer and Edge Hardware? An Empirical Study

limitations: No tagged release; this commit pins the inspected bundle; energy is measured only on Jetson and one MoE exceeds the thesis total-parameter bound.
relevance: Strong reproducibility bundle with raw JSONL, model hashes, pinned llama.cpp, hardware metadata, honest OOM rows, and direct Jetson energy.
title: Edge MoE reproducibility bundle

limitations: Severity classification is metadata-adjacent and narrow; RAG contexts and model runtime conditions need direct inspection; preprint only.
relevance: Directly motivates a cheap RAG x training-type x latency experiment: tiny models can improve sharply while some reasoning models degrade or time out.
title: Benchmarking Small Language Models and Small Reasoning Language Models on System Log Severity Classification

limitations: Multi-agent system and safety claims are benchmark-bound, first-party, and not small-model/CPU evidence; license is noncommercial share-alike.
relevance: Specialized detect/diagnose/mitigate agents, explicit state machine, and Transactional No-Regression sharpen the operation-state and no-regression contract ApprenticeOps can test.
title: STRATUS: A Multi-agent System for Autonomous Reliability Engineering of Modern Clouds

limitations: Chaos-injected microservice datasets are cleaner than production incidents; dataset rights and redistribution require a separate gate.
relevance: Adds process-level localization, identification, and evidence-grounding dimensions to the AIOps benchmark cluster already covered.
title: A Multi-Dataset Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agents in Microservice Failure Diagnosis

limitations: Preprint has no verified durable dataset/code URL in the abstract page; one system and controlled faults limit transfer.
relevance: Separates root-cause accuracy from admissible recovery actions and live restoration, a major gap in the current prose-only ApprenticeOps scenarios.
title: Can LLMs Really Recover Microservice Failures? A Recovery-Aware Evaluation of Diagnosis-to-Action Reasoning

limitations: Preprint benchmark artifact availability and rights need verification before any row import; large deterministic sandbox is outside current node capacity.
relevance: State Snapshot Paradigm makes RCA reproducible and can generate SFT/RL trajectories without mutating production infrastructure.
title: Cloud-OpsBench: A Reproducible Benchmark for Agentic Root Cause Analysis in Cloud Systems

limitations: Five-model OpenRCA study; pitfall attribution to architecture is observational and benchmark-specific.
relevance: Twelve process-level failure labels show incomplete exploration and hallucinated telemetry persist across model tiers; prompting alone is insufficient.
title: Why Do AI Agents Systematically Fail at Cloud Root Cause Analysis?

limitations: Diagnosis/recovery evaluation spans several agent settings and an internal Microsoft prototype; recovery gains require independent reproduction.
relevance: PROBE turns failed-run telemetry into structured diagnosis and bounded guidance, directly matching the need to analyze where an agent fails and whether a retry recovers.
title: Debugging the Debuggers: Failure-Anchored Structured Recovery for Software Engineering Agents

limitations: MCQA prompting changes the response distribution and does not directly transfer to open operational answers; linked code availability requires recheck.
relevance: Answer stability and abstention are adjacent evidence for the planned repeat-disagreement risk-coverage analysis.
title: Second Guess: Detecting Uncertainty Through Abstention and Answer Stability in Small Language Models

limitations: Open issue, not peer review; configurations differ from paper and issue remains unresolved; one contributor promised more context but no resolution is recorded.
relevance: Practitioner reproduction suggests parser, template, runtime and tensor-parallel settings can materially change tool-calling accuracy.
title: Unable to Reproduce Reported Accuracy from Paper

limitations: Single application benchmark and author-run lab; not a controlled independent paper; JAX reference runtime differs from Cactus production runtime.
relevance: A useful negative reproduction: a 26M router failed on a real 20-tool schema due truncation, broken retrieval weights, chat misrouting and latency.
title: Cactus Needle 26M as tool router: benchmark and reject verdict

limitations: Self-reported Show HN with no comparative benchmark; linked paper does not validate Selora efficacy; product/pricing discussion is not scientific evidence.
relevance: Concrete practitioner signal for a 1.7B Qwen base plus four Home Assistant task adapters; useful as a scenario and architecture lead only.
title: Show HN: Selora - local model for Home Assistant
